x: As it was a close match resulted, and grand performances were put up by our sprinters, Jack Frost and Fred Clay, against such opposition, with Jack Brown, our A.A.A. junior 880 yards champion, others giving their usual sterling performances.
Jack Brown is to be congratulated on gaining a stripe. He is at Catterick with the Royal Signals, and hopes to compete in the Army Track Championships this year.

Len Marchant, Vic Blowfield, Albert Frost, Jack Brown and Eric Herbert all gained standard awards, and with the men we have available I think we could take on any club in the country, at say 6 or 8 × 1 mile.

Cope was beaten in the 880 by Kierans in 1 min. 59.8 secs., and Jack Brown won the 1 mile in 4 min. 37 secs. Ted Stimpson showed a glimpse of his old form in winning the 2 miles in 9 min. 52 secs., and we also won the medley relay event.

With the help of Dick Towndrow, and such as Archie Bedford, Eddie Short, Mike Heard, “Ginger” Kennedy and Jack Brown, to mention only a few of our promising members plus the help of last season's stalwarts, I think we shall have yet another successful year over the country.

Our lads had gradually been working their way through the field with Len Marchant always up with the leading bunch, and eventually Mike Heard was 11th with Jack Brown 13th and George Durrant 14th, which was a very good show on their part.

McDonald was the winner and he certainly ran well in his usual determined style and there was a dead heat for second place between Jack Brown and "Ginger" Charlton, which the latter won on the toss of a coin with Brown taking third prize.

When they came in sight again Vernon Blowfield was in the lead with Jack Brown running stride for stride with him, and then, unfortunately, they went slightly off the course, and so came home well in front of the rest of the field.
On the next stage, Jack Brown took us in front and running well clocked 28.7. Len Herbert went off on the 5th stage which had been slightly altered.
John Cope was second to Pugh in the 440 and we had first two home in the 880 in Len Marchant and Jack Brown. Bill Lucas won the mile and Eddie Short won the two miles, beating Ted Stimpson.

In the two miles team race we had the first three home, with Jack Brown, Vern Blowfield and Len Marchant finishing in line. We lost the Medley Relay where John Cope tried hard to hold Nankeville over the first 880 but the Walton man gave his team the lead which they maintained to the end.

Len Marchant completed a double by winning the 880 yards in 2 min. 3 secs. and the mile in 4.31 secs. Jack Brown was runner-up in the mile. Eddie Short won the 2 miles with Reg Ruddick third and we won the team race.

Derek Burfitt had a hard tussle with Martin of Surrey in the mile to win in 4 mins. 27 secs. with Jack Brown third. In the field events, Charlie Melchoir was second in the Javelin and third in the Shot Putt.
Holtum, a new member was second with Johnny Morrison third. The 3 miles run was the main event on the programme with Jack Brown, the back marker off 60 yards and the limit man on 500.
The individual winner was Bill Lucas, and he finished full of running, and was followed home by Ches. Walker and Jack Brown. Mick Porter and Lew Bush also ran well as did J.

Derrick Burfitt then took over and set about the opposition in his usual determined fashion and he eventually handed over to Jack Brown in second place with the Aylesford runner the only one he had failed to overtake.

On the 19th November we had Woodford Green A.C. and the Royal Military Police (Woking) as visitors to Belgrave Hall, for an 8 aside match over our 5 miles cross-country course. Bromley of the Police was first man home just in front of Vern Blowfield and Jack Brown.
At the end of the first lap Vern Blowfield and Derrick Burfitt were running stride for stride in the lead followed by Les Stokell and Jack Brown.
In the recent Civil Service cross-country championship, Derrick Burfitt was placed 3rd, with Eric Herbert 7th, Jack Brown 9th and Rene Howell 11th.
When they came in sight again Jack Brown was out in front followed by Charlton, who was running in borrowed rubbers, then came Bill Lucas and the holder Vern Blowfield came in fourth.

Les Stokell who finished in tenth place was one of these and Jack Brown also came in minus his shoes. Vern Blowfield after making a fast start had a bad time and fell right back but came through again later on to finish in the first 100.
Les Stokell ran his usual determined kind of race while Jack Brown seemed content to take matters easy in front of Archie Bedford, Steve Charlton and Jack Bragginton.

Jack Brown went off next and he mantained our fourth place although losing ground to the Blackheath runner. This was one of the stages where the existing record was broken and Jack's' time was also inside the old record of 27.25.

In the 1 mile, Derrick Burfitt and Jack Brown strode round in the lead and never looked like being troubled and they ran in together. We scored major points in three of the five field events with our Latvian member, A.
There was an entry of 13 teams and although we were without Len Herbert, Jack Brown and Bill Lucas, the latter being down with a touch of 'flu, we nevertheless managed to score a good win.
In the 1 mile it was our turn to score a “ maximum ” and we actually had the first three men home, with Jack Brown leading Vern Blowfield and Ches Walker in the good time of 4 min. 31.4 secs.

Vern Blowfield did 4.31, running first, then Jack Brown 4.34, Bill Lucas 4.46, and Derrick Burfitt 4.34 to come home winners. In the 3 miles Team Race we had Jack Bragginton, George Lucas, Steve Charlton and Len Bishop, but could only manage a 4th place in this event.
Ches Walker ran a good race to win the 880 yards in the fast time of 2 mins. 2 secs., while Jack Brown won the 1 mile race in 4 mins. 32.3 secs.

Odde was third in the 440 and Jack Brown won the 880 yards in 2 mins. 1.3 secs., with Archie Bedford in fourth place. Len Bishop was third in the 1 mile, but Charlie Smart surprised the locals by winning the 2-mile race, in which he beat Broughton, of Blackheath, in the fast time of 9 mins. 29.6 secs.
In the 2 miles run, Bill Lucas ran well off the back mark of 20 yards to go through his field to win in the good time of 9 min. 19.4 secs. Arthur Bruce was second with Jack Brown third.

Thompson, the international runner, and " Mac " clocked 4 min. 33.8 secs., which is good going for a lad of his age. Ches Walker won the 440 yards, with Odde in second place, and Jack Brown won the 880, with Archie Bedford fourth.

The heats of the 1 mile saw Jack Brown and Ches Walker competing and a notable absentee was Derrick Burfitt. Brown ran quite well to finish inside the standard time of 4 min. 25 secs., and Walker also gained standard and actually finished a very close fourth in his heat with the first three only goi…

Jack Brown and Bob Taylor ran for us in the 440, and Ray Tooby did the half for us in the medley relay. Final points were : Southgate H. 47; Victoria Park H. 45; Belgrave H. 33½; Polytechnic H. 24½; Woodford Green A.C. 24.
Derrick Burfitt was not defending his 1 mile Senior title and Jack Brown ran a good race to beat Len Herbert with Bob Taylor gaining his first club championship medal in third place.
Walker third in the 880, while Jack Brown finished second in the 1 mile. Len Herbert won the 2 miles event beating such runners as Lillikas, Doug.
We thus led throughout and with Len Herbert, Derrick Burfitt, Vern Blowfield and Jack Brown to call on, it is a pity that the “ National ” Brighton Relay has been put off until April, 1951.
Jack Brown, however, had other ideas and with a lap to go he went well ahead to win in 15 min. 19.2 secs., with Jack Bragginton just beating Archie Bedford for second place.

Fred Rickards sends best wishes to all and says he hopes to be on the road again soon. In the Civil Service Championships, Jack Brown was second in the 1 mile and Charlie Smart gained a similar position in the 3 miles event.

Bill Lucas came next and he was followed by Jack Brown, Vern Blowfield and Ches Walker, who came in together, with Bob Taylor and Ted Stimpson close behind, and this laid the foundation of our win in the team race over our old and friendly rivals.

Jack Brown on the second leg turned our small deficit into a two-second lead, and from then on we were never headed. Steve Charlton, who came into the team at the last moment owing to Len Herbert being indisposed, ran like a champion on the third stage and eventually handed over with a twenty-eight second lead.

The first lap was slow, with the field well bunched, as our lads did not know the course, but during the latter stages John Bromley, Jack Brown and Bill Lucas took command, although Wells, of the home club, did his best to hang on, closely followed by Jack Bragginton and Ray Tooby.

Jack Brown was prominent on the first lap and eventually ran away from the field and finished an easy winner. Denis Brickwood and Bill Lucas ran steadily throughout the race to finish third and fourth, and were well backed up by the Bishop brothers, who are most certainly our keenest supporters at all our fixtures.

Our first member to finish was Ches Walker, who ran well to finish 7th in such a high-class field, while Jack Brown also did well in finishing 34th and missed by one place being the sixth scoring man for his county, who were placed third.

Jack Brown retained his hold on the trophy although his time was slower than the previous year but conditions underfoot were on the heavy side, if you can apply this remark to our rather light course across Wimbledon Common.

Jack Brown and Eric Herbert also ran well and the latter put up what was easily his best ever performance over the country. Ted Stimpson and Les Stockell completed our team and it was a pity that either of these two were not a little further up as we lost the team title by the narrow margin of 5 points.
Jack Brown running his usual good race regained the lead for us and this was maintained by Len Bishop only for his brother Alan to be forced to drop back into 3rd place.

Jack Brown tackled the long run from Handcross to Hickstead, and ran well, although losing ground slightly to the teams immediately behind us, who were—Thames Valley, Reading A.C., Sutton Harriers and Victoria Park A.A.C.

" Ginger " Holtum won the 100 yards senior event, and Geoff Osmint showed good form in the 220 yards to gain us yet another win. Jack Brown won the half-mile, with Len Bishop in fourth place, and his brother, Alan, finished third in the 440 yards.

The senior match saw " Ginger " Holtum win the 100, with " Paddy " Mullen second in the 220, while Jim Heathfield was third in the 440 yards. Jack Brown was second to Johnny Prince of S.L.H. in the half-mile, with Bob Taylor third, and Chas.
Alan Sexton scored a fine double win in the sprint events, with " Ginger " Holtum runner-up in both races, and Jack Brown was second in the 880 yards, with Bill Lucas winning the 1 mile.
In the straight running events we did well, with Jack Brown winning the half-mile, Reg Bolam taking the 1 mile and Bill Lucas the 3 miles, with Les Stokell in second place.

In the 880 we had both Jack Brown and John Bromley qualify for the final and, although Bromley took the lead with 220 yards to go, with Jack on his heels, they had to give best down the straight, to eventually finish third and fourth.

In the Middlesex events “Ginger” Holtum ran really well to finish second in the 100 yards, and our old member, Derrick Burfitt, won the 1 mile. Jack Brown was second in the Kent 1 mile, with Ray Tooby in third place, and H.

The Southern Senior Championships were held at Reading on June 23rd and our representation was not very large, due to various reasons, but we did gain a couple of third places. Jack Brown ran his best mile to date to finish third to Seamon and D.

Jack Brown also took a team up to Scotland and with himself running the half-mile, Alan Sexton the quarter and “Ginger” Holtum and Geoff. Osmint the two 220's, they duly won the 1 mile relay at Hawick.
In the middle-distance events we did better, with Ian Badiali winning the quarter, Jack Brown the half-mile and Bill Lucas the mile, a very creditable trio of wins.

The one mile senior was the race of the afternoon, with a very strong field turning out, but Jack Brown, the holder, ran a well-judged race to come away over the last 200 yards to beat Len Herbert and Chas.

In the 1 mile event we saw Jack Brown run a fine race to win in the new record time for this contest of 4 mins. 18.8 secs., and then in the 2 miles team race the individual winner proved to be young Ray Tooby, in the fast time of 9 mins. 17.2 secs.

Jack Brown, the holder, was a non-starter, but a small bunch of runners soon detached themselves from the rest of the field with Lucas, Herbert, Tooby, Bromley, Stokell, Bruce and Stearman more or less together.
On the last " leg " Jack Brown was really in form and he went right away from the rest of the field to give us our fifth win out of the last six races on the Brighton Road.

Paterson for first place and Jack Brown was another to finish well up. The Shot Putt handicap was won by Les Stokell who is now taking up field events, he has ideas about becoming a decathion performer, and he certainly did well to take first place in the handicap with Frank Kemp second and a new member in R.

All the first five were selected to run for Surrey in the Inter-Counties race at York, and Jack Brown 7th in the Kent race and A. Cockram 5th in the Wilts. championship, will also be running in this event and this must be almost a record for any club to have seven representatives in such a race.
Jack Brown 51st was running for Kent while a new member in A. Cockram finished 153rd running for Wiltshire.

A good field of 38 runners faced the starter on a snow covered course of two laps, and at the half-distance Charlie Walker was out in front being about 60 yards ahead of Bill Lucas and Jack Brown who were together.
Jack Brown and Len Herbert were 7th and 8th, just ahead of a batch of T.V.H. lads and these forward positions gave us the " edge " in the team race.
On the second lap we saw Charlie Walker, Eddie Short, Jack Brown and Archie Bedford running well together with Bill Lucas, our captain, acting as the whipper-in.

Championships, but Jack Brown with fifth position in the Mile in 4 min. 13.6 secs. (well inside world's record of years ago), and many others gaining standard medals in the various events, ensured that our colours were worthily carried.

Blowfield and Jack Brown were now in the thirties with Walker and Eddie Short also inside the fifty's, but our last two scoring men were still much too far back to stand a chance of securing a place in the team race.

Jack Brown had put in a club record-breaking run on the final leg and his time of 17min. 15secs. beat Pat Parker's old record by 5 seconds. Jack also gained 40 seconds on the leader, and if only we had been a little closer when he took over, who could say what the result might have been.

We had triangular matches with Herne Hill H. and Woodford Green A.C., and in the Senior 100 yards we saw Holtum finishing 3rd, and he followed this with a 4th place in the 220. Badiali was 3rd in the 440 and Jack Brown finished 2nd in the 880 yards with Bob Taylor in 4th place.

In the former event we were in the "A" section of the race with such clubs as Poly H., Achilles, Walton, Herne Hill, and Southgate H., and our team of Jack Brown, Holtum, Sexton, and Badiali did well to gain third place.
Ian Badiali won the 880 yards in fine style, beating Allen of Ealing H., the Middlesex champion, with Jack Brown and Ray Tooby also behind him.

The Kent championships saw Ray Tooby win the Senior 1 mile with Jack Brown in second place and the time was 4 min. 19.6 secs. "Ginger" Holtum was 2nd in the Middlesex Senior 100 yards championship, and Bob Taylor ran well to finish 2nd in the 880 yards.

Bob Taylor and Jack Brown both qualified for the final of the 880 yards, and Bob ran well to finish 4th with Jack in 6th place. As usual, we had no runners in the 120 yards Hurdles, but Don Maclean was 6th in the 1 mile and so scored yet another point.

In the 1 mile we had Jack Brown, Ray Tooby and Don Maclean running for us, and with the first two only to qualify, Jack left nothing to doubt and romped home an easy winner of his heat with Bill Nankeville in second place in 4 min. 16.6 secs.

Jack Brown went next for us and he ran a well-judged race to catch the Walton man down the home straight, but Len Herbert could not hold Nankeville over the final leg, and we finished second in 17 min. 25 secs., which was only just outside the British (National) record of 17 min. 22.6 secs.
Basil Walden won the 100 yds., beating Gibbs, of Herne Hill, and the latter was also beaten by Alan Sexton in the 220. Jack Brown and Ian Badiali were 2nd and 3rd in the 880, and A.
In the 1 mile senior we saw the holder, Jack Brown, retain his title although his time of 4 min. 19 secs. was a second slower than his record time of last year.

Our team also won the 2 miles team race with Jack Brown first man home in the good time of 9 min. 16.4 secs. A certain ginger-haired sprinter also won the 220 yds. event for reserves, and the problem was, I think, how to get all the prizes into the coach for the journey back to London!
After Mike Stearman had shown the way over the first two laps, Jack Brown went in front and simply ran away from the rest of the field, and he lapped over half of them.
Ian Badiali won the 440 yds. in the good time of 51.5 secs., and Jack Brown was second to Terry Higgins in the 880 in 1 min. 57 secs., with Alan Bishop in third place
Jack Brown ran his best mile of the season to beat Gordon Pirie in the fast time of 4 mins. 13.4 secs., which was a record for this meeting and also a personal best for Jack.
On the first stage from Mitcham to Purley we had Jack Brown, and he put up a truly magnificent performance to beat Alec Olney’s record time of 27.37 by five seconds.

Walker going up to him but before very long Jack Brown and Ray Tooby had taken command. This was the order in which they came back to the finishing field and Jack and Ray ran in together for first place with “ Ginger ” Newell showing a welcome return to form in gaining third place.

Among the successes by our members during the past track season were—Ray Tooby who won the Junior Inter-Banks 1 mile race in 4 min. 28.2 secs. Jack Brown 2nd in the Civil Service 1 mile with Bob Taylor 3rd in the 880 yards.

In mentioning the above names we are not attempting to detract from Jack Brown's running in winning the race, as his time was well up to standard and he finished in comfortable fashion in front of Chas.
On 20th December, against the local club, Cambridge Harriers, it was unfortunate that our captain, Jack Brown, turned up just too late to take part in the race.
Truelove, the A.A.A. team manager, was present as a spectator and he must have been impressed not only by Jack Brown's fine running but also by the numbers present.
The race was two laps of our usual 5 miles course, and at the half-distance Jack Brown and Mart Whenman were running together well away from the rest of the field.

In the Senior race over 10 miles there was a field of 371 starters and after the usual fast start, Gordon Pirie and Frank Sando were out on their own, with Dennis Holden also in complete isolation in third place. Jack Brown was running quite well and was only beaten by the three above mentioned, plus Jim Peters and R.
Jack Brown was our first man home, 34th, and so won the Harry Parker Trophy, and he was closely followed by John Bromley, 39th, and John showed a welcome return to his old form once again.

Walker on once again being selected to run for Surrey in the Inter-Counties c.c. race, also to Bob Belmore, who is a second-claim member, and to Jack Brown, who was a scoring member of the Kent team, who were third in the team championship.
Anyway, we have some very good examples in Jack Brown and Bob Taylor. What most young Belgravians seem to lack is pace and judgment, and I should like to see some concentration on them.
Jack Brown, John Bromley, Archie Bedford and Eddie Short were notable absentees, and the first three named were included in our Brighton team, with Eddie as 1st reserve.
Jack Brown won the 1½ miles in another new track record time of 6 mins. 58.2 secs., while in the 3 mile event we had Bob Belmore 4th and Don Maclean 5th.
On the first stage to Purley we had Jack Brown, and he ran well to hand over in second place behind Frank Sando, of Aylesford, in 28 mins. 22 secs.

Jack Brown ran for Kent in the 1 mile, but was unplaced, and Bob Taylor also ran for Middlesex in the 880 yards, but without success. In the so-called "International" events at this meeting, Denis Merrett was second in the 220 yds., and was also a member of the winning team in the mile medley relay.

He had travelled down with the other Poly. runners by car from the White City, where they had been competing in the Caledonian Games meeting and we were hoping that Jack Brown would come down with them in order to run for us in the 2 miles event.
…d 3rd. We also turned out a team for the 2 mile team race at the same meeting and were again placed 3rd, our team being Jack Brown, Chas.…
"Jock" Cameron was 2nd in 51.2 secs., and Jack Brown won the 880, with Frank Wright in 2nd place in 1 min. 59.4 secs. Peter Bagnall was 2nd to Nankeville in a 4 mins. 15 secs 1 mile. and Chas.

Kennedy (130) in third place, and although the scratch man, Jack Brown, started in the race, he retired after a couple of laps. We also had three heats in the 440 yds. handicap and the final saw Bob Wolton just beat C.

In this we were again 3rd to Poly. and Woodford Green, and our time of 3 mins. 25.6 secs. would have won this event in previous years. The race of the evening was the 4 x 1 mile event for the "Victory Trophy," and on the first leg we saw Jack Brown give us the lead.

In the 880 yds. both Jack Brown and Bob Taylor qualified for the final, and we were the only Club with two runners in this. Although Bob ran well he could only get 4th in 1 min. 55.7 secs., while Jack Brown did 1 min. 59 secs.
In the 1 mile we had our big thrill of the evening when Jack Brown won his heat, beating Bill Nankeville in the fast time of 4 mins. 12 secs., a personal best performance.

Owing to Len Herbert crying off with a leg injury, plus the fact that the Civil Service meeting took away Jack Brown, Bob Taylor and Chas. Walker, and Ray Tooby was competing at the Inter-Banks, we were unable to field a team in the 2 miles team race.
The " big " event of the meeting was the Club 3 mile track championship, and the holder, Jack Brown, retained his title in 14 mins. 31.4 secs.

Jack Brown came over from the White City where he had been running for the Great Britain " B " team in the attack on the 4 x 1 mile world's record, and he successfully defended his 1 mile title, beating Chas.

At the Vickers' meeting at Weybridge we again won the " Viking " Trophy, presented to the winning team in the 2 mile team race. John Bromley ran well to finish 3rd, with Jack Brown 5th, Chas. Walker 7th and Bill Lucas was our non-scoring runner.

This was held over the old course from Mitcham to Brighton and Jack Brown put us in the lead on the first stage.Bill Lucas dropped to 3rd on the next leg only for Stan Gawler to pick up a place on the third relay.

Our 7 miles Cross Country Championship for the Blackstaffe Shield was held on 12th December, and was won by Jack Brown, the holder, in the fast time of 36mins. 17secs. 2nd and 3rd places were filled by G.T.
The tit bit of the meeting was the two miles run handicap in which Jack Brown ran a fine race to go right through the field and win in the fast time of 9mins. 6.6secs.

This event which carries with it the Macher Shield was held on January 30th and the holder Jack Brown, made sure of retaining the trophy by scoring a runaway victory in the fast time of 55mins. 9secs.

Jack Brown on his favourite stage from Mitcham to Purley produced another of his excellent performances on this leg and with a well judged effort took Belgrave into a very valuable lead of twenty one seconds from Surrey A.C. and Sheffield.
Our team was weakened by Jack Brown's absence and it is interesting to note that G. Olding, our Second Claim member, who was beaten by Jack in the Club "7", finished 19th.
In the Kent Championships Jack Brown won the mile in 4 mins. 19.6secs and R. Liggins was 2nd in the javelin with 178ft.
Track performances were seriously affected by the track being rain sodden. This was obvious from Jack Brown's mile which he won in 4m. 23s.

We were however still hopeful of a recovery for Jack Brown had been entrusted with the long leg to Handcross. Unfortunately he was not in his usual devastating road form, perhaps due to lack of racing in the weeks prior to this race.
Jack Brown was seen to be not so fit as in previous years and one of the lads running with him said "He ran down to the brook like a plum pudding".
The best feature of the race was the expected tussle between Jack Brown, John Burr and Cliff Roffey, and an exciting battle it was with the three of them coming home within 2 seconds of each other.

Jack Brown then made an effort and moved away from the rest on his way down to the brook, never to be challenged again. He came round 56 seconds in the lead at the end of the first lap and the rest of the field were fairly well strung out with Bedford making his way through from about 11th at 2 miles.

Jack Brown's performance was a little disappointing, but Charlie Walker had obviously recovered from his cold on the "Club" 10 day. Bedford ran a good race and again was seen making his way through the field as the race progressed.

At about 2½ miles Cliff was still leading our team and lying about 60th, Pete Bagnall was next, 83rd with Eddie Patterson 85th, next J. Masters 96th, Dave Baulch 118th, Charlie Walker 120th, Eric Gebbett about 150th, and Jack Brown about 160th.

Smart regained one place and then Jack Brown, with the second fastest time of the day, brought us back to 4th. Burr gained a place but Bagnall was passed by Ken Norris, T.V.H. who did 17.42, the fastest time of the day.

Jack Brown then ran the race of the day, in the lead, breaking the course record by 13 seconds and giving us a lead of 95 seconds. Bedford and Walker then made sure of our victory though Charlie took things a little too easy in the middle and so we missed the course record by one second.

Though his time did not appear impressive, our only man to beat it in post war years has been Jack Brown. At the change over S.L.H. were 75 seconds ahead of us and Jack Brown's course record of 28.21 had been beaten by Ellis, T.V.H. 28.20 who went through to 2nd, and by Llewellyn of Walton, 28.17 wh…
Archie Bedford ran his usual "gutty" race and passed the Aylesford man putting Jack Brown off second 50 seconds behind Laurie Reed S.L.H. junior.
Mayers (Middlesex) reached the final of the 220 yards but were unplaced. Jack Brown (Kent) qualified for the final of the mile with 4.15.4. and was eventually placed 7th.

The race started at a fair pace and at one time it seemed that an upset on form was going to happen when, with one lap to go, Hallowell was running so strongly, it gave Jack Brown the holder, some anxious moments and it was only in the last 100 yards that Jack came away to win in 4m. 23s.

These events have, in former years, been the main attraction for Belgrave supporters but this year we had but one entry (Jack Brown in the mile) in the championships from 880 yards upwards, including the steeplechase, and he was forced to withdraw through injury.
Although saying the three miles was not his distance, Jack Brown ran a splendid race to break the track record with a time of 14mins. 20.8s.
The main events of this meeting on 20th July were the three miles Track Championship and the Hop, step and jump Championship. The first named resulted in a win for Jack Brown in 14mins. 32s. with P.

I would also like to congratulate Jack Brown on notching yet another championship win over the country. Whilst I am not going to go through all the individual performances, one which is definitely worthy of mention is that of Charlie Dabbs in winning the Surrey Youths Championship.

Walker, Jack Brown and Archie Bedford who filled 4th, 7th and 9th positions respectively. Charlie Dabbs, still only a youth, took 10th place, a performance which should not pass unnoticed and it is hoped that his amazing improvement will continue over the next few years.
The remaining strength lay in the excellent packing of Jack Brown, P. Newell and J.Masters who finished 7th, 8th and 9th making a total score of 28 points to Herne Hill's 30, and Hampstead 48.
Jack Brown is to be congratulated on once again getting his name inscribed on the trophy as also are Eddie Short and George Davidson on their 2nd and 3rd placings.
After being the leading Belgrave runner for a considerable distance, Peter Bagnall was passed in the last lap by Jack Brown who ran extremely well to finish 52nd.

The scratch man Jack Brown was unable to get to grips with the field and was timed in at 9mins. 39.2secs in fifteenth position. We cannot keep our Field Events men out of the picture these days and they were busy putting the weight.

Although we knew there would be some non-starters we hoped to have a fairly strong team for this event which was held on a cold and rather windy 14th January, when Eric Gebbett arrived with a cold, Jack Brown failed to arrive at all and our hopes rapidly dwindled.

On the customary last Saturday in January, Jack Brown, for the seventh year in succession, won the ten miles Championship. He was accompanied over the first five miles by Pat Newell, followed by Walker, Bagnall, Short and Gebbett, but at this stage Short retired.
Jack Brown soon passed this club on the third leg and went right away from the field to give us a lead of 63 seconds. George Davidson ran well on the 4th section and put us even further in front.

Jack Brown set off on the long leg to Handcross in steady fashion and soon picked up the 16 seconds we were in arrears of Birchfield. Jack's performance was undoubtedly one of his best and at Handcross we were 5th.
We won the sprint relay, were second in the Medley relay and third in the two miles team race with Jack Brown finishing 3rd in 9mins. 16.8secs.
Minor placings were gained by Jack Brown who was 2nd to Sando in the three miles; Charlie Jones was second to Wilmshurst in the Triple jump.
Jack Brown shook off all opposition except the great Gordon in the three miles dowing an excellent time of 14m. 48s. The result of all these efforts was a win for the Bels. by a clear 10 points.

Jack Brown was our sole competitor in the Championship race and by excellent pace judgment worked his way through the field to take 6th place and become the first Belgrave man ever to beat 14 mins. with 13.59.
It is interesting to note that on the same day as the Championships, Jack Brown competed in the Kent County 6 miles championship and won in a new County record time of 29m. 40.3s.

Jack Brown who had beaten 14 minutes three weeks earlier in the Southern, was competing although not wearing our colours - that vest you wear Jack is most drab compared to Belgrave's claret and gold - and we were anticipating a further improvement on this time.
Jack Brown was not able to run owing to injury and Mike Browne retired also owing to injury. Ron Liggins was third in the Javelin with 184ft. 3ins, this after coming off night duty with no sleep.

On 21st July Jack Brown won the Civil Service 1 mile Championship in 4m. 18.2s. In the Sefton Branker Trophy Meeting on 25th July Brian Hallowell representing the Civil Service was 2nd in the mile and John Davies (Middlesex) was 3rd.
We are already London County Cross-Country Champions and we are pleased to see the great form of Jack Brown, Charlie Walker and Charlie Dabbs.
Club members performed with distinction at Hurlingham, a most noteworthy achievement being Jack Brown's record breaking run in the three miles.

However, our lads put up some sterling performances, the most notable being a record 5000 metres in 14m. 21.8s. by Jack Brown. Mal Ash won the pole vault, high jump and 120yds. hurdles and was placed in the triple jump- what an asset this boy is!
We were weakened again in the senior events, Ron Holtum having the flu and Jack Brown unable to be present. Bob Taylor tried to contact Charlie Walker but failed.

As the Manchester Guardian stated "Jack Brown of Belgrave Harriers........made a startling entry into the ranks of short distance road runners when he took second place to O'Gorman in the Walton A.C. 10 miles event".

On the longest leg of all,Jack Brown ran a "blinder",making up 2 places and 30secs on T.V.H.His time was surpassed only by St. Albans' O'Gorman,at that time well behind us.Jack gave Heywood of H.H.H a fright and was unlucky not to catch him before Handcross.
Once again Jack Brown showed his fitness by winning from A. Towle of Herne Hill after a very exciting struggle throughout the greater part of the race.

The usual cold, misty weather greeted the starters for this year's race, but soon warming to his task, Jack Brown set about the opposition in no uncertain manner and was soon in the leading bunch with Salvat of Finchley and Cameron of T.V.H.

Jack Brown ran very impressively to win by a full minute from Charlie Walker with Ray Tooby half a minute further back in third place. Steve Charlton, showing much improved form, deservedly won the handicap.

Continuing along his road of success Jack Brown sliced off 41 seconds from Jim Peters course record, a most meritorious performance. The race seemed to resolve itself quite rapidly into two fierce battles, between O'Gorman, Brown, Keily, Hicks, Lambert and Haslam on the one hand and a close bunch of…

The field was off to a fast start but it was not until just after the brook that Jack Brown managed to drop Charlie Walker. Coming up to four miles Brown had a lead of one hundred yards on Walker, with Dave Baulch a similar distance adrift, followed by Eric Gebbett and Ray Tooby a little way behind.

Our six scoring men, led by Jack Brown, were all well placed throughout, and whilst commendably they held those placings, one did not see the spectacle of the claret and gold vests moving up through the field in last desperate attempts to whittle away those points.

Jack Brown was lying about 36th with Eric Gebbett leading the rest of the team in about 120th position. A course of this nature however, called for restraint in the early stages, when many spent too much energy endeavouring to move up before they had even allowed the field to settle down.
Our next man, however, Jack Brown, was to have none of this, and proceeded to smash Redrup's record and put us in the lead with a scintillating run.
Ray Tooby moved up to 4th place on the next stage, and Chas Walker, with an almost identical time, ensured that our next man, Jack Brown, was within striking distance of the leaders.
We have temporarily lost the services of Jack Brown. We must make some more silk purses if we are to maintain our high standard of performance in middle distance running.
We were without the services of Jack Brown for this race but still felt fairly confident of winning the team race. Walton A.C. however, had other ideas, and defeated us by four points.
At 5 miles Jack Brown had "lost" the field and looked set for another easy win, Colin Collis followed in 5th position from Chas Walker, Dave Baulch, Eric Gebbett and Len Bishop.

Pride of place goes to Jack Brown for his excellent run on the seventh leg which gave him a stage record. This was made with no help whatsoever as the team in front were well out of sight for most of the leg and those behind were never with Jack.

Pat Newell, taking over Jack Brown's cloak, proved a worthy successor on the hard grind from Crawley to Handcross, and in gaining two places brought us within sight of all but T.V.H. who had widened their lead,through a grand run by Bert Ingles, to 2½ minutes over the second club, Woodford.

With Jack Brown in Cyprus and Colin Collis (temporarily we hope) retired it was to be expected that we would not retain our team title. Our chances were even further reduced when Eric Gebbett retired at nine miles after unwisely trying to stay with the leaders who were moving at a very hot pace.

Jack Brown writes to say how really difficult life has become in Cyprus; the strain on everyone is intense and being practically confined to their house Jack and his wife Betty and son Malcolm find their greatest enjoyment is derived from their record player.
Jack Brown, Arthur Bruce, Len Adams and Ray Tooby all broke stage records, with Eddie Short also doing so but finding one better runner on the day in Ken Norris of Thames Valley.
Most notable of these were the 440 yds. win in 48·7s. by Clive Ryan - a new Championship record, and the mile win of Malcolm Robinson in which Jack Brown's long standing record only just survived.
We hope to welcome Jack Brown back from Cyprus in Mar/April of next year, and it will be pleasing indeed to see him in our teams once again.

Most of the lads are eagerly awaiting the return of Jack Brown from Cyprus. His experience will be most welcome to the newer members of our team, and his return to competitive running could well coincide with the commencement of another successful run of Belgrave performances over road and country.

We have however the prospect of the return of Jack Brown and the further improvement of many of our runners such as David Jones, Malcolm Robinson, Clive Shippen and Charlie Dabbs, plus juniors Alan Black and Ken Miller who move up to the senior ranks to inspire our hopes for 1960/61.
Mal's winning time of 4:15.8 bettered Jack Brown's nine year old mark by 2.2secs, and with six men inside 4.20 this was surely the fastest ever Club mile.
A new Club record of 13:30 set by Jack Brown on the first leg did not survive the afternoon; 30 seconds was lopped off it by Pat Newell on the 5th leg.

Amongst the runners were Ranjit Bhatia, on his last outing from Wimbledon before returning home, Jack Brown, recently returned from Cyprus and already re-establishing himself as a danger man and Cliff Roffey, home on furlough from Kenya.
Jack Brown, making a welcome return to the team, took the fourth stage to Merstham and although losing ground on the leader kept us in 2nd place.
The exception was Jack Brown, now running with much of the fire shown in his pre-Cyprus days, who moved up to 1st place on the fourth of the six stages.
Jack Brown was 21st, Charlie Dabbs (without shoes, à la Tulloh) 32nd, Masters 47th, Dooley 57th, Gebbett(recovering from gastric trouble) 60th and Johnston 64th.
Jack Brown (21.10) was also fairly well up. After these four the field became rather strung out with Hallowell, Johnson and Gebbett filling the next three positions.

Talking of the "Brighton", what a heartening sight it was to see Jack Brown handing over to Ron Linstead! The former has got back into his running most impressively after his 3 year absence whilst Ron has burst into the limelight in most sensational fashion.

Pat Newell was in a class of his own in the Senior event, with Jack Brown a good second; team support was poor however. Cyril Forey (a great prospect) was a comfortable winner of the Junior race with John Thresher third; and our Youth success was due to Hampshire and Fairclough being 2nd and 3rd.

"Evergreen" Pat Newell is running as well as ever these days and we can no doubt look forward to another consistent season from him, while Jack Brown, although getting no younger, is still likely to show a clean pair of heels to his rivals, especially when it comes to relay running.
"We've not a ghost of a chance in the National, but with a bit of luck, and if everybody turns out, we might get placed in the Southern", so said Jack Brown just after the Club '10'.
Jack Brown had the place of honour, but despite the excellent time of 17.53 could do little more than gain on all the teams ahead except Woodford.
Held on March 4th, two weeks before the Ilford, the Bels. got off to a great start when Jack Brown came home a clear leader on the first stage.
Held on March 25th, this was the club championship race for the "Wimbledon" Cup, and Jack Brown was the name to be inscribed under that of Ramjit Bhatia - who set such a hot record last year.

STAGE 8 - Jack Brown (30.25, 10th fastest). Jack protests that he is getting old, but there are few in Belgrave who can hold him on the road; as he proved by lowering Charlie Dabbs stage record by 18 seconds to maintain our sixth position in the face of heavy opposition.

His 8.55 when placed third in the London Club's 2 mile race at the White City erased Jack Brown's mark of 8.59 from the record book. Others to set up personal bests in this event are Malcolm Robinson with 9:08.2, Pat Newell 9:09, Dan Maclean 9:11.6 and John Davies 9:15.
In the A.A.A. 10 miles track championship, held at Hurlingham on 15th April, Jack Brown finished 4th in 51 minutes 11.8 seconds - just 0.8 seconds outside Charlie Dabb's club record.
Jack Brown, who has won this trophy on four consecutive occasions, made every effort to close the gap, but halving it was the most he could manage and so had to be content with second place.

On the third leg, Jack Brown maintained our place with an excellent 13:36, and although he was the "A" team's slowest man, John Thresher (14:09) ran well enough to take us up to second, 43 secs. behind the eventual winners - Polytechnic Harriers.
Jack Brown made a valiant effort to keep the gap as small as possible between himself and the loping Scot ahead, but Bill seemed to have the matter well in hand at all times.

STAGE 8 - Jack Brown (31:50. 15th) Jack took over still in 6th place but 3½ mins. behind Portsmouth. Jack was obviously not at his best, and although plugging along on what is the hardest stage of all, was noticeably losing ground on all teams ahead.

Elsewhere in this Gazette a spotlight has been thrown upon the career of that fine athlete Jack Brown. This was prepared on hearing of Jack's retirement, but he has since told me that the urge to compete again is very strong.
The mid 1920s were not the most pleasant years that this country has known and Jack William Brown was born in 1925, a year before the General Strike.

Eric Gebbett (A) Jack Brown (B) and Ray Conway (C) set off on the first stage and eyebrows were raised when Jack and Eric came down the finishing straight together in 6th and 7th positions - a fine start for both teams.

Pat now holds two Club stage records against Jack Brown's three - this can surely be changed next April Pat! The story of the race is one that almost excludes the winners Portsmouth for they took the lead on the third stage and from then on it was only a question as to how far ahead they would be at Brighton.

TOP LEFT: Eric Gebbett fights out the first stage against Fudge (Portsmouth) and Darbon (Shaftesbury). TOP RIGHT: Jack Brown climbs the airport drag on Stage 3. CENTRE LEFT: Cyril Forey on the Gatwick stage.

Cambridge Road as usual, sorted the sheep from the goats and Barry Sawyer returning once more to the form he showed about a year ago, pulled away from Eric Gebbett and Jack Brown who were renewing the battle they enjoyed in the Poly Relay only a week before.

New faces are always welcome and this season the road running ranks have been swelled by Gerry North, Bill Kerr, Charlie Walker, George Williams John Moore and Peter Wrench; and with Jack Brown showing a return to form, things look good for next season.

Jack Brown had to make full use of his experience to pull back Tony Fairclough and John Davies in the later stages but eventually he got away from them and was fast catching Barry Sawyer in the run in.
But Gerry is a champion and held off last year's winner by 10 yards to provide an even more exciting finish than when Jack Brown pulverised Dennis O'Gorman a few years back.

Jack Brown, who appeared only as a reserve, was a gallant 109th in his first race since the Club '7' in early December. Close behind was Don Maclean (118) who made ground impressively in the latter stages to complete our scoring six.
He works at the War Office where he occasionally teams up with that other Belgrave stalwart Jack Brown in their sports club team. How good it is to see Charlie Dabbs running well again.
Charlie Walker had a good run to give us the lead, 3 seconds ahead of Chelmsford (Hill-Cottingham) and Jack Brown increased this to 14secs with Poly (Proffitt) moving up to second place.
Walker, Jack Brown, or any of his contemporaries they'll tell you that he was one of the closest 'near-misses' that British athletics has had.
In the A.A.A. 10 Mile Track Championships at Hurlingham, Jack Brown finished 9th in 52:26.4 (Intermediate times. 3 miles 15:28.0; 6 miles 31:14.0).

A "ghost" Belgrave team ran in the Wimbledon '10' on the day of the Southern London-Brighton relay and finished 10th. Jack Brown was 27th in 55:18 Norman Stairs 36th in 56:17, Pete Sadler 38th in 56:23 and Bob Glover 46th in 57:12.
Barrie Sawyer regained the lead on the 3rd leg with a good run and this was maintained by Jack Brown, Trevor Hart and Arthur Bruce on legs 4, 5, and 6.
Next to take over was Jack Brown, but not surprisingly he had to give way to 'kipper' Herring who pulverised the opposition, and took Blackheath from 7th into a 100 yard lead.

Jack Brown was 9th in the A.A.A. track '10' at Hurlingham on April, 11th, recording the good time of 54:18.4. At the Herne Hill Winter Floodlit meeting at Totting Bec on March, 25th, John Thresher won the 3,000 metres in 8.37.0 and Danny Wiseman the 660 in 82.7.

With the main pack throughout, he finished strongly just ahead of Jack Brown who is always able to shake up his younger opponents. Mike's improvement is the deserved result of 2 to 3 years of hard conscientious work and his progress will be followed with interest.

With a tremendous effort Gerry took all but 10 seconds off the Pompey runner (Wale) and, although we failed to win, we were able to furnish our last leg runner in the "Brighton" (Jack Brown) with some interesting facts about his probable opponent!

Although Jack Brown (back into the team again after missing a number of Brightons) was our oldest runner;his great experience soon became apparent,for against a Portsmouth newcomer on his first Brighton, he closed the gap rapidly.
Jack Brown ran himself back into the Brighton team in convincing fashion and Bicourt, in only his second crack at the event, showed he will be well to the fore next time.

Despite fine efforts by Gerry North(4th),John Thresher(8th),Geoff.North (14th)and Jack Brown(30th)Belgrave failed to win the team race by the narrowest possible margin- 1 point.Belgrave scoring 56pts to Surrey AC's 55.
Jack Brown and Mike Shingles also ran well to finish 7th and 10th respectively,but we still only managed 2nd team behind Maidstone who packed 3,4 and 5.

Belgrave's Jack Brown was next reserve on call and would certainly not have done worse than this supporting cast. His absence from the race also meant that the Club had gone 9 years without gaining an international vest over the country.

The most impressive runs were by Adrian Major, a youth, and by Jack Brown, almost a veteran. Adrian's relentless pace took him thro' to sixth-fastest time of the day, whilst Jack showed a fine turn of speed to hold off scratch men Black and Hart.

Only 7 of our Brighton 12 were running but they finished well enough up to take our scoring 10 to a narrow win. Jack Brown followed up his memorable relay effort with a fine 17th place,only 17secs behind Tony Fairclough (18 years his junior).
Jack Brown also ran well and will no doubt be picking up many Vets prizes come his 40th birthday in August. John Dear,Don Maclean and the "Dukes Joggers" completed our two teams. 153 finished.

Mike Shingles, who had been below his best for several weeks, was unable to break through the spell and dropped us to 4th on the next stage- a position maintained by Jack Brown on the 3rd leg, and who regained much lost ground in closing up to within 13secs of the runner ahead.

Only 4 of our expected six appeared and Jack Brown and Don Maclean were moved up to fill the gap. Both ran very well, but we were obliged to concede 53 seconds to Blackheath at the end and had to be content with 3rd place.

Trevor Hart ran well on the Redhill stage and kept his place, although losing a little ground on Coventry, and when Jack Brown (40 this year!) took over on the short leg Coventry were only 37 seconds ahead.
Jack Brown showed the rest of the field a thing or two, beating his old rivals Newell and Walker and dusting up those young "upstarts" Bicourt, Dear and Major!

Of the others Doug Brew ran very well in his first attempt at the distance to finish in 67th place. Mike Bullivant broke Jack Brown's course record by over a minute but it should be remembered that conditions were ideal.

…shing behind 20 years old Reilly was a runner exactly twice Joe's age - that elder statesman of the running fraternity, Jack Brown. Jack moved well away from his immediate rivals on the final lap and clocked a time that placed him 5th in the handicap - form that suggests he will be running yet again…
Their last man was few places in front of Charlie Walker - perhaps Jack Brown may have a twinge of conscience for withdrawing just to let Charlie run !
It was good to see Ranjit Bhatia showing some of his old form again and with Jack Brown and Pat Newell also putting in useful appearances the team was not unlike those of 7 or 8 years ago.

Once again veteran Jack Brown put in another of his stirling performances, shaking up many first team aspirants with his 29:27; and Ranjit Bhatia made the most of his years stay in England by re-appearing in the race for which he once held the record (27:56 in 1960).
Overheard in the dressing room:- "The reason that Jack Brown remains so fit is that his son is now running so well over half a mile that Jack has to make sure he doesn't beat him!
Jack Brown went through the field like a dose of salts with 3 mile splits of 15:40 and 15:31 to beat Ranjit Bhatia who was competing in his last track race before leaving again for India in October.
His struggling effort left him over two minutes behind our first man, Peter Whewell, and dangerously near that old Belgrave favourite, Jack Brown.
Also to Chas Walker, over 9 mins faster than his time last year - what would he do if he started training again !! (Jack Brown please note !!!)
North takes the platform on "Timekeeping today". Jack Brown speaks on "Putting back into athletics what you get out".
Jack Brown

This was the match we've been waiting for, a 5 Mile cross country race at Hayes against the veterans of Blackheath with the added interest of the meeting between Jackie Brown and Charlie Walker brought together for the first time as Vets by the Cross Country Secretary through devious means known only to himself.

JACK BROWN is alive and well and winning mile races! Our star of yesteryear, who was in international class at everything from one to twenty miles, raced in the event at which he started out when competing in the veteran's mile at the Carshalton Trophies meeting in April.
Taking the lead, which he held to the end, is Len Marchant who won in 1:59.0 from Len Herbert (4th from right) and Jack Brown (6th from right).
He followed this up by beating all the juniors for the 'Savage Shield', beating all the seniors, bar Jack Brown, in the 'Blackstaffe Shield' seven miles, and finishing 2nd in the Surrey Youths.

The individual winner was Bill Lucas, and he finished full of running, and was followed home by Chas. Walker and Jack Brown. Mick Porter and Lew Bush also ran well as did J.H.Braggington, who is a first season runner over the country.

In the over 50 event 2nd claim member Jack Brown (Cambridge H) was the winner in 36:13. The Belgrave team scored 61pts for 7th place with E.Young 23rd in 41:23, Joe McDonald 31st in 42:26 and John Baker 44th in 43:47.
In the Club Championships of 1955 he ran in the 1 mile and clocked 4:27 for 3rd place behind Jack Brown's 4:23. Brian Hallowell, who was to become John's training partner and rival, placed 2nd.

We had triangular matches with Herne Hill H and Woodford Green AC and in the Senior 100 yards we saw Holtum finishing 3rd, and he followed this with a 4th in the 220. Badiali was 3rd in the 440 and Jack Brown finished 2nd in the 880 with Bob Taylor in 4th place.

In the Club Championships at Battersea Park Jack Brown came over from the White City where he had been running for the Great Britain "B" team in an attack on the 4 x 1 mile world's record, and he successfully defended his 1 mile title, beating Chas.

In 1949 the first two men home, Vernon Blowfield and Jack Brown went slightly off course and were effectively disqualified but Verne took the record down to 29.09 in 1950, and following the cancellation of the 1952 race through snow bound roads, Ray Tooby opened up the 28 minute era with 28.50 in 1953.

We did, however, have Jack Brown in 6th place in the Kent Championship. This situation was confirmed a few weeks later in the Inter-Counties, our first scorer in 52nd place being Bill Lucas - Surrey's third man.
The Club Ten Mile Championship following the Counties was won by Jack Brown from Charlie Walker and Bill Lucas, confirming our hopes for the big races ahead.

On the next stage to Merstham, Ted Stimpson held his place ... then Frank Abberton tackled the uphill stage through Redhill and ran a fine race to take us up to 2nd place. On the next stage Jack Brown took us in front.

I well remember a very agitated Jimmy Green (Editor of Athletics Weekly) running up to me saying 'There's an unknown runner up ahead running in an un-numbered white vest. He took over from Jack Brown so he must be one of your's.
This was followed by 3rd in the Southern and 6th in the National with the lead man on each occasion being Jack Brown with Charlie Walker, Len and Alan Bishop, along with Dennis Brickwood in the team.
Bob Taylor equalled the Middlesex record held by the great Arthur Wint in the 880 yards, and Ivan Mayers beat Ron Holtum in the sprints while Jack Brown won the Kent one mile.
The year started with the road runners winning the Mitcham 15 led by the individual winner Jack Brown. Then followed a third place in the Southern race at Epsom.
Belgrave Harriers regret to announce the death of John “Jack” Brown who passed away on 24 September in his 84th year. He had spent his last years in a nursing home.
